2#![allow(missing_docs)]
3use crate::int::{NInt, PInt};
4/**
5Type aliases for many constants.
6
7This file is generated by typenum's build script.
8
9For unsigned integers, the format is `U` followed by the number. We define aliases for
10
11- Numbers 0 through 1024
12- Powers of 2 below `u64::MAX`
13- Powers of 2 minus 1 below `u64::MAX`
14- Powers of 10 below `u64::MAX`
15
16These alias definitions look like this:
17
18```rust
19use typenum::{B0, B1, UInt, UTerm};
20
21# #[allow(dead_code)]
22type U6 = UInt<UInt<UInt<UTerm, B1>, B1>, B0>;
23```
24
25For positive signed integers, the format is `P` followed by the number and for negative
26signed integers it is `N` followed by the number. For the signed integer zero, we use
27`Z0`. We define aliases for
28
29- Numbers -1024 through 1024
30- Powers of 2 between `i64::MIN` and `i64::MAX`
31- Powers of 2 minus 1 between `i64::MIN` and `i64::MAX`
32- Powers of 10 between `i64::MIN` and `i64::MAX`
33
34These alias definitions look like this:
35
36```rust
37use typenum::{B0, B1, UInt, UTerm, PInt, NInt};
38
39# #[allow(dead_code)]
40type P6 = PInt<UInt<UInt<UInt<UTerm, B1>, B1>, B0>>;
41# #[allow(dead_code)]
42type N6 = NInt<UInt<UInt<UInt<UTerm, B1>, B1>, B0>>;
43```
44
45# Example
46```rust
47# #[allow(unused_imports)]
48use typenum::{U0, U1, U2, U3, U4, U5, U6};
49# #[allow(unused_imports)]
50use typenum::{N3, N2, N1, Z0, P1, P2, P3};
51# #[allow(unused_imports)]
52use typenum::{U774, N17, N10000, P1024, P4096};
53```
54
55We also define the aliases `False` and `True` for `B0` and `B1`, respectively.
56*/
